title: Least privilege and default-deny
one_line: Secure defaults are least-privilege: default-deny network policy, authenticated ingress, scoped RBAC, non-privileged containers, and pinned image tags.

worked_examples.context: DNS resolves but pod-to-pod traffic between two namespaces times out.
steps: Recall that a default-deny NetworkPolicy is expected, so cross-namespace traffic needs an explicit allow.
Look for the missing allow policy rather than assuming a DNS or routing fault.
Apply the narrowest allow rule that unblocks the required path.
worked_examples.result: Diagnose the missing allow policy under default-deny, and fix it with a minimal, scoped rule.

constraints.must: a remediation grants the narrowest permission/allow needed, not a broad one
constraints.violated_feedback: You proposed a broad grant (wide RBAC, allow-all policy); scope it to the minimum required.

misconceptions.belief: a connectivity timeout is usually DNS or routing
misconceptions.correction: Under default-deny, a timeout with working DNS often means a missing NetworkPolicy allow rule.

misconceptions.belief: using the :latest image tag is convenient and harmless
misconceptions.correction: Unpinned :latest tags make deployments non-reproducible and are flagged as an insecure default.
